A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DQ-A retrieval-attack research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval-attack experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and empirical topic-clustering verification, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds injection-position, reranking, perplexity, transfer-verification, runtime, and document-boosting results.

M1.justification: The principal DQ-A procedure and objectives remain unchanged. Section 6 develops v1's suggested loss reversal into a tested boosting variant, additionally replacing the maximum over sampled queries with a minimum.

E1.justification: The four BRIGHT domains and synthetic 24-topic corpus are retained. v4 adds an evaluated document-boosting task within economics and tests beginning and middle injection scenarios beyond the original suffix setting.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains GCG, PRADA, and Poisoned-RAG, while Table 3 retains S-GCG and DQ-A-H. The additional rerankers are victim-system configurations; the perplexity analysis does not introduce a competing attack method.

E3.justification: The original benchmark protocol is retained, but substantial additional protocols appear: two retriever-reranker pipelines with candidate pools of 25/50/100, perplexity comparisons against corpus thresholds, conditional transfer verification at margins 0 and 0.05, and a boosting test that relabels all economics queries to one selected document.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component, query-count, and token-length ablations, v4 adds injection-position sensitivity, reranker robustness, perplexity screening with an attacked example, empirical transfer-theorem verification, computational-cost analysis, and a boosting case study. These substantially expand the supplementary evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the random-seed prompt recipe is unchanged. The new transfer-verification percentages are empirical outcome rates rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 3 and all original topic-verification values are unchanged. v4 adds results in Figure 7 and Tables 4-7, covering injection position, reranking, runtime, transfer rates, and perplexity. Its new boosting experiment reports Recall@50 increasing from 0.00227 to 0.00601 within that experiment, not an improvement over v1 under the original setting.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.2 becomes a theorem with explicit independence and positive-margin assumptions. New Appendix A supplies a proof and a two-element-topic approximation derivation. v4 also formally defines the perturbation distance and introduces an asymptotic computational-complexity expression.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: query-agnostic black-box document suppression, a topic-clustering framework, adversarial query-document learning, and transferability across retrievers. The added experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 substantially extends practical interpretation: injection-position effects are attributed to attention, reranker vulnerability to first-stage document exclusion, and weak perplexity separation to short injections within long documents. It also qualifies the boosting effect as limited and discusses majority-voting defenses as future work.

D1.justification: Table 5 newly discloses a timed configuration of 20 epochs and 10 injected tokens, averaging 23.065 seconds per document; acknowledgments identify NCSA Delta GPU resources. Prompts, dataset statistics, and repository access are retained. These disclosures do not establish a change to the original experimental budget.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations concerning ranking manipulation, perplexity defenses, and possible defense adaptations, including Xing et al., Du et al., Alon and Kamfonas, and Hu et al. The existing related-work taxonomy and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Changes include light abstract and terminology editing, new experimental subheadings, acknowledgments, and insertion of proof and additional-experiment appendices before the original appendix material.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 7 and Tables 4-7, restyles existing schematics, and reorganizes several displays. Table 1 is shortened, while Table 9 consolidates the original full Qwen, Gemma, and Jina topic results into one table. This is a substantial display expansion and restructuring.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new position, reranking, and perplexity analyses provide useful practical evidence, and runtime disclosure improves transparency. The gains remain limited: Appendix A.1 uses a maximum over victim-model similarities while Eq. (5) states a minimum over surrogate-model similarities, leaving the claimed theoretical bound unresolved. The narrow perplexity comparison also supports less than a general conclusion about defense effectiveness.
